https://www.dw.com/en/thailand-several-k.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IQWu The number of people killed and injured in the shooting remains unclear Image: Athit Perawongmetha/REUTERS Advertisement Several people were killed and others injured in a shooting at a high school in Thailand's Nonthaburi province, north of the capital city of Bangkok, local authorities said. Students, teachers and other workers were evacuated from school as authorities deployed police officers, rescue workers and emergency doctors to the scene. According to the police, the gunman, who is a student at the school, first fatally shot his grandparents with his grandfather's handgun. Then, he went to his school and killed three teachers and three students before killing himself. Earlier, Thai national police spokesperson Trairong Phiwphan said that 15 people were wounded. In a statement, police said the gunman fired 26 rounds, and an additional 34 rounds of ammunition were found at the scene. Students, teachers and other staff members were evacuated from the school Image: Chalinee Thirasupa/REUTERS Meanwhile, Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul expressed his condolences and stated that he had instructed relevant officials to assist those affected. School shootings in Thailand The incident took place at the Debsirin Nonthaburi School in ​the ‌Bang Kruai district of Nonthaburi. According to district authorities, the Debsirin Nonthaburi School had an enrollment of around 3,100 students and 147 teachers in the 2025 academic year. Thailand has one of the highest rates of gun ownership in the region. It is estimated that around 10 million firearms are in circulation, or about one for every seven people. In February, a 17-year-old stole a gun from the police and opened fire at a public high school in southern Thailand . The two-hour attack resulted in one death and two injuries. https://nineoclock.ro/bcr-provided-more-.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Banca Comercială Română (BCR) provided €535 million in financing during the first eight months of 2026 for energy sector projects in Romania, of which €360 million was allocated exclusively to renewable energy generation capacities. The installed capacity financed during this period amounts to 948 MW, comprising 780 MW of renewable energy capacity and 168 MW of storage capacity. The projects financed by BCR between January and August 2026 alone are expected to generate approximately 1.6 TWh annually, equivalent to more than 3% of Romania’s final electricity consumption. Overall, BCR is currently part of financing structures for energy projects totaling 3,020 MW, at various stages of development, construction and operation: 2,033 MW of wind power; 552 MW of storage capacity , of which 168 MW are standalone projects and 384 MW are integrated into hybrid projects; 435 MW of photovoltaic capacity , of which 295 MW are standalone projects and 140 MW are part of hybrid projects. “Over the past six years, we have tripled BCR’s financing in the energy sector, starting from the premise that energy is the infrastructure on which Romania’s competitiveness, our ability to attract investment and companies’ confidence that they can build their future here all depend. The approximately 3 GW included in BCR’s financing structures show that Romania is moving from intention to construction. Our role is to bring together capital, financial expertise and investors capable of turning projects into actual generation capacity,” said Bogdan Cernescu, Corporate Banking Director, BCR . The 2026 financing comes against the backdrop of a fundamental transformation of BCR’s portfolio. In 2020, BCR’s exposure to the energy sector stood at €930 million, concentrated predominantly in oil and gas. By August 2026, the energy and utilities portfolio had reached almost €3 billion, of which 69% represents utilities and renewable energy, while financing for wind, photovoltaic and storage projects alone exceeds €1 billion. In recent years, BCR has supported more than 2,600 MW of new renewable energy capacity, alongside investments in transmission and distribution networks and critical infrastructure. “The volumes we have today are a signal of how the market is evolving. Six years ago, we were predominantly financing oil and gas. Today, two out of every three MW we finance are wind power, while almost one in five MW is storage capacity – exactly what the system needs to operate effectively. BCR is the leading banking partner for energy projects in Romania, and we continue to support investments in new generation, storage and distribution capacity through financing structures tailored to complex projects and their various stages of development,” said Manuela Trisnevschi, Head of Energy and Utilities, BCR . The most recent transaction is the financing of the Urleasca wind farm , with a capacity of 77 MW, developed by Scatec ASA. BCR and Erste Group are providing €132 million in financing, of which BCR’s contribution amounts to €76 million. In 2026, BCR also announced financing for the following renewable energy projects: Peștera II wind farm , Constanța County, with a capacity of 392 MW, through €151 million in financing provided by BCR–Erste Group; Dobrun and Sadova photovoltaic projects , developed by Scatec in Dolj and Olt counties, with a combined capacity of 190 MW, financed by BCR with €42.5 million; Săcele wind farm , Constanța County, developed by Greenvolt Power, with a capacity of 49.8 MW, through €58.5 million in financing provided by BCR–Erste Group; Gura Văii–CEE Onești wind farm , Bacău County, with a capacity of 49.8 MW, financed by BCR with €47 million. Beyond the volume of financing, BCR’s portfolio highlights four structural changes in the energy market: Projects have grown significantly in size , with Peștera II being one of the largest wind investments in Romania; Experienced international investors , such as Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, Scatec and Greenvolt, are accelerating their move into the construction phase; Financing is becoming more sophisticated , bringing together investment loans, VAT facilities, credit lines, guarantee instruments and hedging solutions tailored to the entire project lifecycle; Bank syndication is the way to enable investments at scale , with the speed at which a group of banks can be formed around a project being a key factor. BCR’s largest exposures within syndicated financing structures currently range between €100 million and €150 million per transaction . https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/.text: Military Menu Introduction Systems Facilities Agencies Industry Operations Countries Hot Documents News Reports Policy Budget Congress Links WMD Intelligence Homeland Security Space Military US Spy Aircraft Flies for 9 Hours Along Russia's South Over Black Sea - Flight Data 20260910 MOSCOW (Sputnik) - A US reconnaissance aircraft, a Bombardier ARTEMIS II, on Thursday spent nine hours in the air over the Black Sea, circling southern Russia, according to flight data analyzed by Sputnik. The plane took off from Romania's Mihail Kogalniceanu airbase at around 05:45 GMT and started patrolling at around 6:10 GMT. The flight was carried out about 100 kilometers (62 miles) from the Russian coast, the data suggested. As of 15:05 GMT, the aircraft was completing its third lap along the coasts of Crimea, the southern Russian regions, and Abkhazia and was landing in Romania. On Thursday, its route differed from the usual one: it returned once, approaching the territory of Romania in order to turn around and fly along the southwestern part of Crimea. It usually stays above the sea, as data have shown. Bombardier ARTEMIS II, converted by US company Leidos from a business jet for radar reconnaissance. It is often used to patrol the skies around Russia's Kaliningrad Region. According to publicly available information, only two of these aircraft were built for the Pentagon. They are designed primarily to intercept, record, and decrypt data over long distances. In recent years, Russia has been flagging up NATO's unprecedented activity and buildup of troops near its western borders. The Kremlin has stated that Russia does not threaten anyone, but would not ignore actions that are potentially dangerous to its interests. © Sputnik
